question: Is species-specific chorus memory localized to the exact physical SiteID, or does prior strong use of nearby route sites predict reactivation equally well?
population: Physically stable matched pairs with prior history; focal species are route-new in the wet survey and had CallingIndex 2-3 at >=1 physical SiteID somewhere on the same route-season stratum strictly before the focal pair.
unit: pair x focal species x physical SiteID

predictors.exact_prior_strong: 1 when focal species had prior CI2-3 at the exact SiteID.
predictors.nearest_prior_strong_distance: Great-circle distance from focal SiteID to the nearest SiteID on the same route-season with prior focal-species CI2-3; exact memory has distance 0.
predictors.route_spacing_normalization: Divide distance by that route's median geographic distance between consecutive StopNumbers, then use log1p.

primary_design: Within each pair x species, demean wet_strong, exact_prior_strong, and normalized log-distance. Regress demeaned wet_strong on both predictors without intercept; cluster covariance by State x RouteNumber.
primary_prediction: Exact-site coefficient >0 with complete 95% CI >0 after the distance gradient is included.
secondary: Distance coefficient <0 indicates spatial decay away from prior strong-chorus sites.
minimum_gate: At least 500 informative pair x species groups, >=250 routes and >=20 species, with within-group exact-memory variation and finite route spacing.
interpretation: Support identifies an exact-site component beyond neighborhood proximity.
It does not distinguish persistent local population from species-specific microhabitat preference.
No individual site fidelity, continuous occupancy, breeding success or causal rainfall claim.
